messages:
Mina R: Starting thread to resolve trade-offs for the console observability beta. We need a prioritized list that balances customer value vs ops cost.
Carlos V: Customers want three concrete things: (1) cost line-items by API route and model, (2) quick error grouping with redacted examples, (3) simple way to see if a model rollout caused latency regressions.
Jo P: UX note: small customers dont care about a million filters; give them a single "top offenders" view + an advanced filter panel. That reduces frontend work.
Eli H: Infra reality: raw span storage is the cost driver. Two levers: sampling policy and span retention. We can either keep sampling high and retention short, or retention long and sampling low.
Mina R: Proposed prioritization buckets:
- Must-have (beta): per-route token cost CSV export, model_version tag in traces (structured), error groups with 3 examples (7d retention).
- Nice-to-have (stretch): clickable raw-span drilldown, 30d aggregated retention, SLO alert binding in console.
- Deferred: per-token attribution at sub-request granularity, full trace linking across services.
Carlos V: For billing reconciliation pilots, CSV export is the top priority. We can hold on raw-span drilldown as long as they can get exports to S3 for deeper analysis.
Jo P: For the UI, I'll prototype a single-page "incident snapshot" that shows top routes, cost spike chart, and an error group preview. That should cover 70% of pilot asks.
Eli H: Sampling policy suggestion: default = sample-on-error + reservoir sample based on per-route QPS (e.g., reservoir size = min(1000, qps*2)). Provide per-customer override. Also auto-boost sampling for 1h after a model_version change.
Mina R: Legal check: any example request shown must have PII redacted and model prompt content scrubbed for regulated pilots. @legal-bot can you confirm minimal redaction rules?
legal-bot: legal: confirm. Required redactions: personal identifiers (names, emails, SSNs), full user prompt text for regulated pilots. We can allow truncated prompts and anonymized tokens. Export to customer S3 requires signed access and retention policy agreement.
Carlos V: Implementation plan (rough): backend tagging + cost rollup (2 sprints), CSV export + S3 write (1 sprint), tracing header + sampler (1 sprint), error group UI + snapshot page (2 sprints) -> ~6 sprints. Can we do a 4-sprint compressed plan if we cut the snapshot page to a template and outsource CSV formatting to an existing export microservice?
Jo P: We can deliver a template snapshot (no custom widgets) in 1 sprint. That frees up time for backend work.
Eli H: Ops constraint: keep raw spans 7d for beta. Aggregated metrics 90d is acceptable. Longer raw spans would require extra infra spend.
Mina R: Acceptance criteria for pilot signoff:
```
- Customer can download per-route, per-model CSV for a 30-day window
- Console shows a "snapshot" with p99 latency, error rate, and token spend for top 5 routes
- Error group page shows 3 redacted examples and a link to export raw spans to S3
- Model rollouts are visible as timeline annotations and can be correlated with p99 spikes
```
Carlos V: Important: model_version must be stored as an enumerated tag (no freeform). We'll limit recorded versions to the last N releases per customer to keep index sizes sane.
Jo P: For the UI disclaimer: "Sampled traces. Limited retention. Use CSV/S3 export for full audits." Short and visible.
legal-bot: Also include a checkbox for regulated pilots: "I confirm exports will comply with my company's retention policies."
Eli H: Action items and owners:
- Carlos: cost rollup + enumerated model_version tag design (due Thu)
- Jo: snapshot template mock + UI disclaimer copy (due Wed)
- Mina: pilot acceptance checklist + comms (due Fri)
- Eli: sampling defaults + S3 export retention flow (due Tue)
ops-bot: ops: obs-canary deploying 04:30 UTC tomorrow; will alert #eng-oncall on failure.
Mina R: Timeline decision: ship beta to internal QA in 4 sprints if we compress UI to templates and reuse existing exporters. Otherwise target 6 sprints. Which do we prefer?
Carlos V: Push for 4 sprints with the template approach. Customer impact for CSV + structured tags is highest.
Jo P: Agree. Templates + strong export path = better ROI.
Eli H: Ok, well aim 4 sprints but keep one sprint buffer for oncall issues. If infra hits snags, we revert to 6-sprint plan.
Mina R: Consensus: 4-sprint beta with explicit limits (sampled traces, 7d raw spans, structured model_version, CSV export + S3). We'll document trade-offs in the beta FAQ.
Carlos V: +1
Jo P: +1
Eli H: +1
legal-bot: +1
Mina R: I'll write the RFC and acceptance checklist and ping pilots. Thanks everyone.
